character.lede: A white modern house stands on a knoll above the water, with a glazed tower between the entry block and the garage. Two flights of stone steps climb to a parapet-walled entry, and a raised terrace holds cascading pools.

spots.line: A writing desk, a gaming chair and a lamp make the small study.
A grand piano, a sofa and a loveseat share the living room.
A house bed and a low bookshelf make Yuna's room.

facts.style: White modern on a knoll: a three-band glazed tower between a lower entry block and a shed-roofed garage wing, thin charcoal slab roofs, two jogged flights of stone steps to a parapet-walled entry, a raised stone terrace and cascading pools in curved tropical beds

character.truths: The Core sits on a credenza in the Living Room, in sight of the door. There is no television. The kitchen has a breakfast bar. Terrace with cascading pools and an outdoor kitchen.

details.rule: every beat of an adult or teen persona (13 or older) gets a detail (before, after, steps, fact); pair beats first

forgejo: [note] Gitea does the same job. Name one Git host per household, not both.
[note] The listing mentions Forgejo Actions CI. The package ships the forge and its database only, no runner, so do not show a CI run.
[claims] Say where the repositories are (on the Core). Do not say it syncs with, or is compatible with, GitHub.
Listing says "fully self-hosted and private": over-claim, do not repeat.
Listing mentions Forgejo Actions CI, but no runner ships: never show a CI run.
mstream: Description says "from anywhere", "completely private" and "no data collection": absolute and remote claims, paraphrase
pi-hole: [claims] Network-wide blocking at DNS. Do not call it parental control or promise safety.
Blocks ad, tracker and bad domains at DNS: not parental control and no promise of safety
Unblocked lookups are forwarded to an upstream resolver (the upstream demo dashboard lists a public DNS, dns.google), so a DNS provider still sees them and it is not offline
Overlaps AdGuard Home: one per household
grocy: [note] The listing is short. Describe pantry stock, shopping lists, recipes and chores only.
Short listing: describe pantry stock, shopping lists, recipes, tasks and habits only (catalog)
Upstream demo screenshot shows a dollar total: prices on screen
donetick: [cloud-link] Notifications use Telegram or Pushover. Both are outside services.
NFC-tag completion needs a phone that reads NFC on the home network
paperless: [note] AI features are off by default. If you turn them on they can use a local model.
[note] Office document conversion is not wired up in this build; OCR and archiving of PDFs and scans works.
syncthing: [qa] No QA screenshot on origin/main (e2e/screenshots). It is listed and installable, but nobody has recorded a verified run.
frigate: [hardware] Needs IP cameras that stream over RTSP. Cameras are not part of the Core.
[public-access] Watching cameras from away from home is remote access, which the sheet leaves unfinished.
[claims] No detection-speed or accuracy numbers. Do not say it prevents anything.
QA screenshot shows "No frames have been received, check error logs": reject. The store listing image shows a real backyard photo that is not a Hub capture.
Watching away from home is remote access: not claimed.
home-assistant: [hardware] The Hub package runs without privileged host mounts. Integrations that need direct USB, Bluetooth or D-Bus access (a Zigbee stick, for example) are not enabled by default.
[note] Ships with a Matter server container alongside. Its manifest sets host_access true because that container uses host networking; no USB, Bluetooth or D-Bus access is granted.
[claims] Do not promise energy savings. Home Assistant has no energy figures in the listing.
Matter container uses host networking (host_access true); no USB, Bluetooth or D-Bus access is granted, so no Zigbee stick.
The QA capture is the onboarding page (shows the product, no data).
hoppscotch: Without sign-in, collections stay in the browser, not on the Core
Heavy for a client tool: three containers
project-nomad: [public-access] Ships without authentication. For trusted home networks only. Never describe it as exposed.
[note] amd64 only (fine on the Core). Internet is needed once for setup and downloads.
[claims] Educational content comes from third-party sources. Do not promise grades.
Ships without authentication: home network only, never described as exposed.
Needs the internet once for setup and downloads; never "fully offline" or "anywhere".
libretranslate: [note] Works offline once language models are downloaded.
Listing says "works fully offline": banned wording (sec-offline)
Likely already heavy in the existing stories
koodo-reader: marketplace: Listing text says nothing is sent to a cloud service; the reader has outside-calling features (translation, lookup, speech).
docuseal: [claims] Do not call signatures legally binding.
[note] Signers outside your home network need access to your Core.
Do not call signatures legally binding
jotty: Public share links need outside reach
Everything is Markdown and JSON files, no database
aider: [cloud-link] The Hub injects its own model endpoint, so it needs no cloud key. A model override field can point it at another OpenAI-compatible endpoint; leave it on the Hub model. A coding agent is private only on the C
[claims] Never claim parity with a hosted coding model and never a speed figure. Every edit is a git commit, which is the approval step: the person reviews and can undo it with git.
[note] The browser interface is marked experimental upstream. Do not call it finished.
[note] Added 2026-10-15 for the builder archetype: the old cloud-or-developer exclusion lumped it with apps that need cloud keys; this one is wired to the local model.
[qa] No QA screenshot on origin/main (e2e/screenshots). It is listed and installable, but nobody has recorded a verified run.
cyberchef: Listing says nothing pasted is ever sent anywhere and that it works with no internet connection: do not repeat either (sec-never-leaves, sec-offline)
A tool, not a store of anything: nothing is held after the tab closes
kokoro: [note] OpenAI-compatible speech API. No GPU requirement in the listing.
OpenAI-compatible speech API; web player included.
No GPU requirement in the listing; no speed claim.
Capture is real (FastKoko player) on a dark purple background.
excalidraw: [note] amd64 only. An Excalidraw MCP entry exists for agents.
marketplace: Manifest source points to ozencb/excalidraw-persist, a 105-star wrapper, not excalidraw/excalidraw.
hermitstash: Listing claims post-quantum encryption and that every field is encrypted: do not repeat (sec-absolute)
Public Drop page lets visitors upload without an account
privatebin: Footer of the screen says the server has "zero knowledge": do not repeat
Overlaps Cryptgeon and Enclosed: one per household
adventurelog: [qa] No QA screenshot on origin/main (e2e/screenshots). It is listed and installable, but nobody has recorded a verified run.
radicale: [qa] No QA screenshot on origin/main (e2e/screenshots). It is listed and installable, but nobody has recorded a verified run.
no QA screenshot (the app has a bare web page)
sync away from home is not claimed
photoview: [cloud-link] Map view uses a Mapbox token you can add. Leave it off for a fully local gallery.
[qa] No QA screenshot on origin/main (e2e/screenshots). It is listed and installable, but nobody has recorded a verified run.
Public sharing links need inbound reach: keep out of stories
Face recognition is a feature, not a claim to amplify
